commits.edited_message:
[sdf] Fix use-after-free in `sdf_generate_with_overlaps`.

When a glyph is rendered with `FT_RENDER_MODE_SDF` while the `sdf`
module's `overlaps` property is enabled, `sdf_generate_with_overlaps`
processes each contour on its own bitmap.  For every contour it calls
`sdf_generate_subdivision`, which in turn calls `split_sdf_shape`; the
latter frees the original contour (`sdf_contour_done` -> `FT_FREE`).
After the call returned, the loop still wrote through the freed pointer
with `contour->next = temp_contour` and then read it back via
`contour = contour->next` to advance -- a heap use-after-free (an
8-byte out-of-bounds write, CWE-416) reachable from a crafted font.

The value read back is already held in the `temp_contour` local, so the
restore write serves no purpose and is unsafe.  Drop it and advance the
loop with `temp_contour` directly, so the freed `contour` is never
dereferenced after the subdivision call.

* src/sdf/ftsdf.c (sdf_generate_with_overlaps): Do not write to or read
from `contour` after `sdf_generate_subdivision` has freed it; use the
saved `temp_contour` to continue the iteration.

* src/smooth/ftgrays.c (gray_convert_glyph): Reserve one band-map
head per contour so that closing a contour does not split a short
band.

Fixes #1445.

(cherry picked from commit efc07621de9c4b8dc2f11032e52ad86eddbbdbdf)

Co-authored-by: Hyunwoo Kim <hw@hwhw.kr>

* src/smooth/ftgrays.c (gray_raster_render): Fix the pool estimate.

The horizontal extent was taken from `min_ey` instead of `min_ex`.
Count both axes.  With that corrected, the empirical factor of ten
double-counts the long side; five cells per perimeter pixel still
covers the CJK glyphs that motivated the original estimate.

Fixes #1449.

* src/cid/cidload.c (cid_read_subrs): Limit overlaps.

Overlaps between subroutine dictionaries can be useful but prone to
abuses. The arbitrary limit can be adjusted in the future. Fixes #1457.

* src/smooth/ftgrays.c (gray_convert_glyph): Reserve a band-map head
for each outline point as well as for each contour.

coupling: gray_convert_glyph sizes the y-bucket map and gray_raster_render sizes the cell pool, and the two were changed in different commits. 98c0d6c reserves one map head per contour and keeps band bisection on the real bitmap height, which still fits while the pool is ten cells per perimeter pixel (a TCell holds three pointers). d5b6bfa keeps the min_ex typo fix but drops that factor from ten to five, which still covers a height-only map. 6bded10 reserves one more head per outline point, which still fits in the original ten-times pool on its own. Any two of those edits overflow the heap block on the same outline: contour heads with the five-times pool, point heads with the five-times pool, or both head reservations with the ten-times pool. Reverting any single edited diff leaves the other pair, so this FT_Outline_Render input still writes ycells[] past the allocation. None of the three hunks is an out-of-bounds write by itself; the repair has to put the map length and the pool estimate back on the same contract.
